source_snapshot.items: Boot Order - Set boot option to BIOS
source_snapshot.procedure: Verify BIOS host interface/network settings, set EFI BIOS boot, read bootparam 5, restart into BIOS and observe flag clear.
source_snapshot.criteria: Node enters BIOS and option matches setting.
source_snapshot.script: Private boot-order-set-boot-option-to-bios; 10 attended and 30 machine minutes; source requests log clearing.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL IPMI setup/readback with inline credentials; operator must visually confirm pre-OS entry.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION at HIGH risk; protected one-time setup mapping, visual marker, no-change exit, auto-clear and order restoration.

historical_reviews.deepseek: It correctly retains human visual confirmation but cannot prove exact vendor mapping, BIOS prerequisites, setup entry, no saved change, clear timing or recovery; its output also incorrectly calls for a PATCH response.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly separates command readback from visual BIOS proof and requires exit without saving plus complete boot restoration.
historical_reviews.history: No earlier exact source identity record exists.
historical_reviews.v3_1: Bootparam proves requested firmware behavior, not that setup UI was reached. BIOS entry is inherently pre-OS and stateful: the operator must identify the intended screen and prove no variable was changed or saved before returning to normal boot.

original_test_intent: Apply a one-time EFI BIOS Setup override, visually prove entry to the intended firmware UI without modifying settings, verify the flag clears and return the node to its unchanged normal boot path.
original_method: Verify exact target, vendor setup mapping, BIOS prerequisites and BootOrder baseline; set/read only the protected one-time override after approval; reboot and capture POST/KVM entry marker; perform no edits, exit without saving, then verify flag consumption, unchanged BootOrder and OS/BMC health.
manual_activity: An operator visually confirms the approved BIOS screen, makes no changes, exits without saving, handles recovery and owns the final verdict.
required_inputs: Host Interface and Network Stack precondition semantics
safety_requirements: Do not edit or save BIOS settings
Stop on wrong screen, firmware prompt, persistent flag or boot timeout
Use independent recovery and never auto-retry
agent_execution_scope: Verify target, setup mapping and baseline
Record operator visual attestation and exit-without-save
engineer_actions: Exit without save and control recovery

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: IPMI setup plus bootparam is relevant if vendor-supported, but inline secrets, inconsistent PATCH narration and absent visual/no-change/clear/restoration proof make it incomplete.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use protected supported one-time setup control, then require operator KVM confirmation, no-change exit and post-boot flag/order comparison.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The 10/30-minute estimates, BIOS checks, restart and 60-second +/-10% note remain subject to vendor confirmation; logs are not cleared.

modernized_recommendation.status: VISUALLY ATTESTED ONE-TIME BIOS SETUP ENTRY
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Correlate protected override/readback with POST/KVM screen capture, operator no-change checklist, exit-without-save event, flag consumption and persistent BootOrder diff.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds an explicit visual oracle and configuration-integrity proof around the pre-OS step.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Bootparam alone cannot demonstrate BIOS UI entry or prove firmware variables remained unchanged.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Entering setup can pause unattended boot indefinitely and accidental save can persist unrelated settings; bounded observation and recovery are mandatory.

project_override_considerations: The Project must define the visual marker and whether BIOS prerequisite changes are outside this row. Any intended firmware setting edit requires its own approved test and restore plan.
expected_evidence: Approved target, setup mapping, prerequisites and normal boot baseline
Protected one-time override and bootparam readback
POST/KVM capture of the intended BIOS screen
Consumed flag, unchanged BootOrder and restored OS/BMC health
Preserved logs, recovery actions and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, procedure and criteria consistently target one-time BIOS entry. Source preconditions support that target and do not prescribe a conflicting boot destination.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Vendor mapping, visual marker, console access, reboot approval and recovery are normal prerequisites; execution blocks only if they cannot be established safely.

review_improvement: Prevents command readback from masquerading as BIOS entry and adds configuration-integrity, safe-exit and restoration evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: Firmware setup entry has no reliable OS-side proof because the normal OS deliberately does not boot. The authoritative observation is the expected KVM screen on the exact node. Since setup UI also grants persistent configuration control, acceptance must pair entry proof with no-change/exit-without-save evidence and a final BootOrder comparison.
